line: Hi, we're Team Byte Code, and this is Paradox, our idea for the security track of VoyageHack.

Here's the thing about B2B travel. The bugs that cost real money don't look like bugs. A refund that pays out twice? The server says two hundred, OK. Same with a fare the agent sets themselves, or one agency reading another agency's passports.
Scanners look for bad inputs. We look for outcomes that should be impossible.

Paradox starts with just what TBO gives us: a staging link, a few test accounts, some recorded traffic and logs. No API docs. From that, it works out the routes, how people actually book, who owns what, and where the money sits.
Then it plays with those journeys the way a sneaky user would. Cancel twice. Skip the payment. Set your own fare. Pretend to be another agency.

After each try, it checks twelve simple rules. Your wallet can't end up richer. The same booking can't get cheaper. One agency never sees another's data. If a rule breaks, that's a finding. If not, it stays quiet.

Like this one. Cancel a booking that's already cancelled, and the wallet gains seven thousand seven hundred and seventy-six rupees. Every single time. Paradox ran it three times to be sure, and cut it down to just four requests.
Every booking it creates carries fake details: a made-up name, email and passport. If those turn up in another agency's account, the leak proves itself.
Each finding turns into a ticket for the team that owns that code, with what it costs in rupees, the exact steps, and how to fix it.

And it keeps watching. When a new release went out, Paradox tested the changed part first. The new amend feature trusted whatever total the client sent. It was flagged as critical about twelve seconds later.
Once the fix shipped, Paradox re-ran its proofs, and the fixed tickets closed on their own.
Along the way, it maps every endpoint, even an old version one route nobody remembered, which was still leaking passports.
Does it work? We planted a hundred and seventy-two random bugs. Paradox found all of them, with zero false alarms. A regular scanner found about thirty percent.
We also tried it on an airline platform it had never seen. After two small, general fixes, it caught all seven planted bugs, and stayed silent on the clean version.
And it's careful. It stays in scope, only touches its own test bookings, slows down if the server struggles, has a kill switch, and logs every request.
That's Paradox. It catches the bug that makes money appear, before someone else does. Thank you.
